description: Cod is a tender white fish that picks up the flavors it cooks with. The sweet flavor from the tomatoes, zucchini combined with the saltiness from the olives will make this Mediterranean-inspired seafood meal a sure favorite.
serving_size: 1 cod fillet + ½ cup of vegetables
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F.
Place tomatoes, zucchini, and onion in a large baking dish, and season with salt and pepper. Drizzle with olive oil, and roast for about 20 minutes or until vegetables are tender.

Remove from oven, and stir in garlic, olives, and basil. Place cod fillets on top of vegetables, and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Drizzle with lime juice. Return to oven. Bake for about 15 minutes, until fish is cooked through.

title: Perfect Sautéed Carrots
description: It may be bold, but we think these are the perfect way to sauté carrots! Slightly caramelizing the carrots adds a delectable richness and sweetness to this simple recipe and is sure to be a hit with the whole family.
ingredients: 1 lbs carrots (peeled and cut into 2–3-inch sticks)
steps: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add the carrots to the skillet, spreading them out in a single layer.
Sauté the carrots for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Season the carrots with the salt, thyme and black pepper.

title: Braised Collards, Potato & White Beans
description: The classic Italian peasant dish, beans and greens using fresh collard greens and cannellini beans and a little spice from red pepper flakes. A delicious side dish or light lunch.
serving_size: 1 1/2 cups potatoes and greens per serving
ingredients: 1 tbsp white vinegar ((white vinegar, white wine vinegar, or apple cider vinegar))
1 small yellow onion (cut into large chunks)
1, 15 ounce can reduced sodium white beans (cannellini or Great Northern) (drained and rinsed)
steps: To prep the collards: Run each leaf under cold running water to clean. Slice the rib from the center of each leaf and chop the leaves into small pieces. Discard ribs. Add chopped leaves to a large bowl and cover with water; add a splash of vinegar. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Heat a large heavy pot (such as a Dutch oven) over medium heat and add the oil.
Add the onions to the pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften, 4–5 minutes.
Add drained collards and cook, stirring occasionally, until wilted, 3–4 minutes.
Add potatoes, oregano, tomatoes, and water. Cook on low heat, slightly covered, for 20–30 minutes, until potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in white beans. Garnish with crushed red pepper if desired.

title: Sweet and Spicy Dipping Sauce
description: This dipping sauce is perfect for egg rolls, chicken wings, crispy tofu, or crab cakes and is a cinch to make!
ingredients: 1 tsp Thai style chili garlic sauce (or other hot sauce)
steps: To make, combine 1/2 cup reduced sugar apricot preserves with 1 Tsp. Thai style chili garlic sauce (or other hot sauce) and 1 Tsp. reduced sodium soy sauce in a bowl and
Heat in the microwave for 30 seconds.

title: Spinach and Feta Egg White Omelet
description: This light and flavorful omelet is filled with sautéed vegetables and tangy feta, served alongside sprouted whole grain toast for a fiber-rich, balanced meal. Using mostly egg whites keeps the saturated fat low, while still offering satisfying protein. It’s a great breakfast option for people with diabetes looking to keep blood glucose (blood sugar) steady without sacrificing flavor. This is a DASH (Dietary Approach to Stop Hypertension), vegetarian recipe, low fat and low carb recipe.
ingredients: 4 slice sprouted whole grain, Ezekiel 4:9 flourless bread, low sodium
steps: Place eggs and egg whites in a medium bowl. Whisk together with black pepper, garlic powder, and smoked paprika.

Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add red onion and bell pepper. Sauté for 2–3 minutes until softened. Stir in the spinach and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until wilted. Remove vegetables from the skillet and set aside.

Wipe the skillet clean and spray the skillet with cooking spray. Return to medium-low heat. Pour 1/4 of the egg mixture into the skillet, tilting to spread it evenly. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the edges are set. Sprinkle 1/4 of the cooked vegetables and 1 teaspoon of feta cheese on one side of the omelette.
Gently fold the omelet in half and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until fully set. Transfer to a plate and repeat for the remaining omelets. Lightly toast the bread slices.

title: Turkey and Bean Burrito Bowl
description: This Turkey and Bean Burrito Bowl offers a balance of protein, fiber, and fresh ingredients, making it a wholesome and delicious meal. Making a burrito bowl removes the carbs from a tortilla wrap.
ingredients: 1 cup black beans (Low sodium, drained and rinsed)
1/8 cup Reduced fat Mexican blend cheese (Shredded)
1 whole lime (Cut into wedges for serving)
steps: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and cook the ground turkey until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon as it cooks.
Add the chili powder, cumin, paprika, kosher salt, and black pepper to the skillet and cook for 3 minutes to toast spices.
Add the bell pepper and onions and cooked until softened. Add in the diced tomatoes and stir well to combine.
Simmer the mixture for about 10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the ingredients to heat through.
In a separate skillet, warm the rice and black beans together.
To assemble each bowl, layer ¼ cup brown rice, ¼ cup black beans, ½ cup lettuce, and about ½ cup of the ground turkey mixture.
Top each bowl with about 1 Tbsp of the shredded Mexican blend cheese and chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

title: Fish Tacos
description: Who says Mexican food can’t be healthy? This recipe proves it can be healthy and delicious! Impress your guests with this quick and easy dish. You can use any firm white fish for this recipe, or even extra-firm tofu for a vegetarian option.
ingredients: 1/2 cup salsa or pico de gallo
1 1/4 lbs firm white fish, such as tilapia or halibut
steps: In a medium bowl whisk together the salsa, lime juice, cilantro, chili powder, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Coat a large sauté pan with cooking spray. Sauté fish over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side. Pour salsa mixture over fix and sauté an additional 3 minutes.
Remove the fish from the pan and flake with a fork, mixing in the salsa mixture.
In a small bowl combine the yogurt and hot sauce. Evenly divide the fish among 8 tortillas and top each with a dollop of the yogurt sauce.

title: Crock Pot Chicken Cacciatore
description: This is an easy recipe for classic chicken cacciatore. It’s perfect for the quick cook looking for a tasty budget-friendly option.
ingredients: 6 oz tomato paste (6-ounce, no salt added)
steps: Place all the ingredients in a crock pot.
Cook on high for 4 hours.
Serve the chicken over whole wheat rotini pasta if desired.

title: Whole Wheat Irish Soda Bread
description: This whole wheat Irish soda bread is hearty and simple with a slightly nutty flavor. It comes together quickly without yeast, making it a great option when you want fresh homemade bread to enjoy with meals or as a snack.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine whole wheat flour, all purpose flour, baking soda, salt, and raisins.
Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients and buttermilk all at once. Fold the ingredients with a rubber spatula until just combined. Do not overmix.
Turn the dough out onto the parchment paper and form into a round loaf. Cut an X into the top of the dough with a sharp knife about 1/2 inch deep.
Place on the middle rack to bake for 30 min or until firm and golden brown.

description: Nutrition information for Peanut butter

title: Spinach Sautéed in Garlic and Oil
description: This “recipe” is so simple, but it’s an easy, healthful and tasty way to cook fresh spinach. Vegetables of any kind—cauliflower, broccoli, peppers, potatoes and/or green beans—can be blanched until just tender, and prepared the same way.
ingredients: 2 1/4 lbs spinach (trimmed, well washed and dried)
steps: Heat the oil over high heat in a very large skillet until very hot. Add the spinach (you may need to work in batches) and cook, stirring, for about 1-2 minutes; the spinach should turn bright green and wilt slightly. Add the garlic and red chile flakes and continue to cook, stirring constantly, until the garlic begins to release its aroma, approximately 30 seconds.
Remove the spinach from the heat, and season with salt and pepper. Toss well to combine, and serve with lemon on the side (for squeezing juice over the spinach).

title: Creamy Chicken & Broccoli Basil Pesto Salad
description: Enjoy a fresh take on chicken salad without breaking the bank. This diabetes-friendly dish is budget-friendly and a great option for lunch or a light dinner. Try pairing it with whole grain crackers to add some crunch to your meal.
serving_size: ¾ cup chicken salad + 2 cups greens
ingredients: 2 tbsp Juice of Lemon (from 1 small lemon)
1/4 cup reduced fat olive oil mayonnaise
steps: Juice the lemon into a small bowl with the shallot. Let sit for about 10 minutes.
Combine the chicken and broccoli in a medium bowl.
Add the pesto, mayo, salt, and pepper to the bowl with the shallot and lemon juice. Whisk to combine and pour into the bowl with the chicken and broccoli.
Serve the chicken salad over mixed greens and cherry tomatoes.

title: Strawberries, 1 cup
description: Nutrition information for Strawberries

title: Budget-Friendly Tuna Pasta Salad
description: You could try this tuna salad without the pasta and serve it on a bed of lettuce or on top of a hearty salad. This quick and budget-friendly meal makes a healthy lunch or dinner.
ingredients: 11 oz flavor fresh tuna (pouch in water)
steps: Cook pasta according to package directions, omitting salt. Drain pasta and rinse under cold water.
In a medium bowl combine remaining ingredients. Add pasta and toss to coat. Serve.

title: Fresh Corn, Tomato, and Avocado Salad with Shrimp
description: Author Aviva Goldfarb got this delectable recipe from Shawn Askew, who works at Bella Bethesda hair salon. This recipe really peaks in the spring and summer, when fresh, farmer's market veggies help the shrimp and avocado shine. Serve with whole-wheat dinner rolls and you've helped solve the "Six O'Clock Scramble" for the perfect diabetes-friendly meal!
ingredients: 1 lbs shrimp (med or large, peeled and deveined)
2 whole ears corn (kernels sliced off (no need to cook if it’s fresh sweet corn. If not, steam it for 3 minutes))
3 oz feta cheese (reduced-fat, cubed, or use Mexican queso fresco or cotija)
1/4 tsp black pepper (freshly ground, or to taste)
steps: DO AHEAD OR DELEGATE: Cook and refrigerate the shrimp, halve the tomatoes, remove the corn kernels from the cobs, or fully prepare and refrigerate the salad (wait to chop and add the avocado until just before serving).

Pan-fry, steam, or grill the shrimp until they are pink, 3–4 minutes total. (Meanwhile, warm the rolls, if you are serving them.) Combine all the ingredients except the shrimp in a large serving bowl. Serve the shrimp on top of the salad.
FLAVOR BOOSTER Add 1/4 teaspoon celery seeds or cumin and 1 tablespoon fresh lemon or lime juice to the salad.
